objective: Use published QSP/M-QSP feasibility characterizations to gate future synthesis requests and keep unknown-channel QSVT oracle costs separate from static-matrix fixtures.

sources.title: Polynomial time constructive decision algorithm for multivariable quantum signal processing
sources.scope: Necessary-and-sufficient decision for the paper's specified pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials, with constructive parameters.
sources.non_claim: Does not certify arbitrary algorithms, hardware implementation, application semantics, energy, cost, or quantum advantage.

sources.title: An adversary bound for quantum signal processing
sources.scope: Characterizes univariate QSP protocols in the stated state-conversion setting; multivariate feasibility implications are theorem-scoped.
sources.non_claim: Do not describe a multivariate feasibility implication as a complete necessary-and-sufficient test unless the theorem establishes that.

sources.title: Singular value transformation for unknown quantum channels
sources.scope: Specified black-box channel model and approximate block encoding of a Hermitized Liouville representation; reported query bounds O(d^3/delta) and Omega(d/delta).
sources.non_claim: Bounds do not establish practical speedup, cheap hardware, readable classical memory, or universal applicability to all QSVT workloads.

canonical_control.interpretation: Existing univariate fixture remains unchanged; M-QSP and unknown-channel results do not retroactively upgrade its evidence.

lane_review.A: Proposed pre-synthesis feasibility gate; current univariate fixture remains regression control.
lane_review.B: No provider calls; future unknown-channel path must freeze oracle/query and target assumptions.
lane_review.C: Keep Hilbert-space dimension separate from readable classical memory; add host/state/I/O accounting after lowering.
lane_review.D: No device requirements until native decomposition and target-aware resources are available.
lane_review.E: BIO-001 and FUS-001 remain evidence-gated; no new material, fuel, net-electricity, or cooling measurements.
lane_review.F: Separate feasibility, synthesis, query, compile, and accepted-task cost; no cost advantage measured.
lane_review.G: D/G co-design receives validated native-gate/control requirements only after A/B/D gates.
lane_review.H: Strategic and financial interpretation remains downstream of measured engineering/economic evidence.
lane_review.I: Auxiliary manifest lane; does not replace or suppress permanent A-H architecture.

foundational_programs.FND-001: No wall-plug energy or erasure measurement added.
foundational_programs.FND-002: No output-information lower-bound change; dimension is not readable storage.
foundational_programs.FND-005: No QFT/particle mechanism or anomaly established.
foundational_programs.FND-006: Mathematical feasibility tools only; no new physical law.
foundational_programs.EQN-001_to_EQN-006: No new physical equation proposed or promoted.

mission_effects.INV-030: No Pangola material substitution or elemental transmutation claim.
mission_effects.INV-031: No accepted liquid-energy product or full-cost result.
mission_effects.INV-032: No net reliable fusion-electricity or lifecycle-cost result.
mission_effects.INV-033: No measured principal, interest, WACC, or time-to-evidence effect.
mission_effects.INV-035: Preserves proof/algorithm feasibility as distinct from empirical physical-law validation.

required_steps: Freeze polynomial fixtures, domains, variables, operator counts, and expected classifications before implementation.
Retain Batch-056 univariate regression and its existing numerical certificate.
Implement the published M-QSP decision algorithm from the full mathematical specification with pinned dependencies.
Cross-check feasible/infeasible cases and constructed parameters against an independent theorem-scoped check.
Record counterexamples, deterministic replay, wall time, host resources, and all failed attempts.
For unknown-channel QSVT, separately record d, delta, oracle assumptions, query count and diamond-norm criterion.
Only then lower to provider-neutral IR and collect target-aware native-gate, memory/I/O, accepted-output, energy and same-target cost evidence.
next_gate.falsifier: The gate fails a known feasible/infeasible fixture, is not deterministic, or provides no measurable reduction in wasted synthesis/compile resources under a frozen matched set.
next_gate.acceptance_rule: A feasibility pass permits only the next software gate; it does not imply physical execution, useful-output acceptance, advantage, or a new physical law.
